It extended ../tsconfig.base.json, and the Docker build proved that wrong. The image builds
with ./server as its context, so the root file is not present, and tsc answered
`TS5083: Cannot read file '/tsconfig.base.json'` and then silently fell back to its own
defaults -- target ES3. The build did not fail on the missing file; it failed on a hundred
cascading errors like `Private identifiers are only available when targeting ECMAScript 2015
and higher`, which points at node_modules and says nothing about the real cause.
A package whose build depends on a file outside its own directory is not independently
buildable, and this repository already decided that server and web are independent (see the
note in the root package.json about npm workspaces). web/tsconfig.json was already
